decision: throttle never loses the final state: trailing write, tab close (pagehide) and page switch each land the last position, page switch on the old page
why: the throttle delays the trailing write
evidence: get_board after a drag ending inside the window: +120/+60 exact; probe build with a 5 s interval: no flush trigger 0 at 1 s and -60 at 6.5 s, tab close +60/+30 at 1 s, page switch -60/-30 at 1 s with the second page empty

decision: tombstones (isDeleted) whose updated is older than 24 h are removed by Y.Map.delete when a room loads; browsers treat a removed key on their page as a deletion of the shown element
why: deleted elements kept their full body (freedraw points included) forever in every save, open and IndexedDB copy
evidence: e2e: one 152-point stroke tombstone 2,849 -> 1,101 B stored; arena probe mix 264,034 -> 27,505 B; offline client reconnecting after a prune hides the element on the new build and keeps showing it on the base build

decision: prune by key delete, not by rewriting tombstones to a skeleton
why: a skeleton is a new Yjs write and loses a concurrent offline undo whenever the server's clientID sorts higher; a key delete creates no item
evidence: arena judge reconnect probe, 2000 random-clientID trials each: undo lost none 0, skeleton 964, delete 0

decision: get_changes does not report pruned deletions; description says a cursor older than a day may miss deletions older than a day
why: reporting them by id re-reported each one to every later cursor (cursors keep only clients that wrote a live value); keeping deleters' clients in the cursor grows it without bound against the 4096-char since limit
evidence: live run: id-only deletion returned again for a cursor taken after the prune; changes.test pins the no-report behavior

decision: the load-time prune is published to peers and other instances but not saved; the next real edit's save stores it
why: every save sets board.updatedAt, so a read-only open, share viewer or agent get_board would mark the board 'Updated' and reorder the dashboard (both reviewers)
evidence: e2e: read-only get_board after the tombstone expired: 3,410 B stored, tombstone kept, updatedAt unchanged; next edit: 2,002 B, tombstone gone, updatedAt bumped; hub test asserts zero saves for a prune-only load

decision: interrogate (reviewer + task seats) on the branch: acted on prune-not-an-edit, pruneTombstones tolerating non-object values, stale TTL comment, untested absent-key rule (now incomingFor in merge.ts with 5 tests), tautological page-switch test removed, real-clock test moved to a fake clock, throttle moved onto the Session; noted cancel-on-denial (same as before) and client-clock skew of the 24 h window
why: contested design (id-only get_changes reverted) and an explicit review gate
evidence: final build: absent-key ghost removed on reconnect, 61 frames for 122 moves on a 2 s drag

decision: schema files have owners enforced by depcruise: board.ts only features/board, auth.ts features/auth plus the shared profile reader, account.ts shared plus features/notification; the two legacy allowances name their expiry (steps 4 and 6)
why: step 3 of docs/architecture/contexts.md: a context must not read another context's tables
evidence: redproof check: 18 rules held; redproof prove: each owner rule fires on a planted import outside its owner

decision: ports are declared in application/ports (or shared/application/interfaces), never in infrastructure; IBoardDocumentStore and IOutboxStore moved; a redproof gate scans for I-prefixed interfaces under any infrastructure folder
why: oxlint 1.90 has no no-restricted-syntax and depcruise matches dependencies, not declarations, so a small scanner gate does it
evidence: server-ports gate: planted interface in infrastructure fails the gate; current tree passes
